description: The state-owned Maxwell Wildlife Refuge has free-roaming bison and elk visible from the refuge roads — a drive-through wildlife experience in the Kansas Flint Hills.
tip: The elk rut (September-October) brings bugling bulls to the roadside. Driving slowly increases wildlife sightings dramatically.

name: Little Jerusalem Badlands Road
description: Little Jerusalem Nature Preserve protects Kansas's largest chalk spire formation — the gravel road to the preserve passes Monument Rocks (a National Natural Landmark) of white Cretaceous chalk.
tip: Monument Rocks is free and roadside accessible — the chalk spires rise 70 feet from flat prairie. Little Jerusalem is a short hike from the parking area.

name: Cheney Reservoir Scenic Loop
description: Cheney State Park's loop roads around Kansas's largest reservoir by surface area — flat but consistently open with lake views and cottonwood-lined shores.
tip: The western shore dam area has the best panoramic views. Spring (April-May) brings large flocks of white pelicans — an unexpected sight on the Great Plains.

name: Cedar Bluff Reservoir Road (K-147)
description: The Smoky Hill River valley around Cedar Bluff Reservoir has the most dramatic western Kansas scenery outside the Red Hills — white Niobrara chalk bluffs and blue reservoir water.
tip: Cedar Bluff State Park is uncrowded. The chalk bluffs on the south shore of the reservoir are directly accessible from K-147.

name: Wilson Lake Scenic Roads (K-232)
description: Wilson Lake is often called 'the jewel of Kansas' — clear blue water surrounded by red cedar and Greenhorn limestone bluffs for an unexpectedly beautiful inland sea.
tip: The south-side roads off K-232 have the most dramatic bluff exposure. Post Rock Scenic Byway continues east from Wilson Lake into the best limestone fence-post country.

name: Lovewell Reservoir Area (K-14 Spur)
description: The roads around Lovewell Reservoir in north-central Kansas — wide-open tallgrass country approaching the Nebraska Sandhills with consistent big-sky driving.
tip: Combine with the K-14 drive north toward Mankato through the Republican River valley for a full north Kansas day. Population density approaches zero.

name: Red River Gorge Scenic Byway (KY-715)
description: Winds through the Red River Gorge Geological Area with sandstone arches, cliff-edge driving, and the most popular rock climbing in the eastern US directly roadside.
tip: The tunnel section near Miguel's Pizza (climbing community hub) is a highlight. Late October foliage here is exceptional.

name: Natural Bridge State Park Road (KY-11)
description: Climbs to Natural Bridge State Resort Park through the Daniel Boone National Forest with forested ridge crossings and roadside sandstone formation views.
tip: The park road past the lodge to the skylift terminal is the tightest section. Combine with KY-715 (Red River Gorge Byway) for a full Red River Gorge day.

name: Cumberland Falls Scenic Byway (KY-90)
description: Follows the Cumberland River through the Daniel Boone National Forest to Cumberland Falls — one of the largest waterfalls east of the Rocky Mountains and the only moonbow site in the Western Hemisphere.
tip: Full moon nights at the falls produce a visible moonbow in the mist — plan the drive for the full moon. The river road section west of the falls is most scenic.

name: Pine Mountain Scenic Drive (US-119/KY-160)
description: Pine Mountain is Kentucky's longest continuous mountain — the road along and over it connects the coal country of eastern Kentucky through genuine Appalachian ridge driving.
tip: The combination of US-119 through Lynch and KY-160 to Breaks Interstate Park creates a full mountain day with the deepest gorge in the US at the end.

name: Black Mountain Road (KY-160, Harlan County)
description: Climbs to the highest point in Kentucky at Black Mountain (4,145 ft) on a road through the heart of Appalachian coal country with genuine mountain switchbacks.
tip: The road is narrow and undivided above 3,000 ft. The summit has a fire tower and views across Virginia — the only place in Kentucky to see mountain ridges stacked to the horizon.

name: Breaks Interstate Park Road (KY-80)
description: The 'Grand Canyon of the South' — Breaks Interstate Park straddles the Kentucky-Virginia border with a 1,600-ft gorge of the Russell Fork River. The rim drive delivers genuine canyon exposure.
tip: The Towers Overlook has the best gorge view — a sheer 1,200-ft drop. The Kentucky side of the park loop is tighter and less-visited than the Virginia side.

name: Carter Caves Scenic Byway
description: Through the cave and arch country of northeastern Kentucky — a rolling forest road connecting Carter Caves State Resort Park with a landscape full of natural arches and sinkholes.
tip: X Cave and Cascade Cave are accessible from the state park with a guide. The arch at Smoky Bridge (off the main road) is roadside accessible.

name: The Trace (Land Between the Lakes)
description: The central road through the Land Between the Lakes National Recreation Area — 40 miles of car-free parkway between Kentucky Lake and Lake Barkley with no traffic lights, no development, just forest.
tip: The Elk and Bison Prairie (north section) has free-roaming elk and bison from the car. The road is divided and smooth — perfect for enjoying the complete absence of commercial signage.

name: US-25E Cumberland Gap
description: The road through the historic Cumberland Gap — Daniel Boone's gateway through the Appalachians — with the gap itself at 1,650 ft and the ridge road delivering views of three states simultaneously.
tip: The Pinnacle Overlook road (above US-25E in the National Historical Park) is a 4-mile steep climb to a 360-degree three-state view — Tennessee, Virginia, and Kentucky simultaneously.

name: Daniel Boone National Forest Scenic Drive (KY-80)
description: The south-central section of the Daniel Boone National Forest combines river access roads, ridge crossings, and the Yahoo Falls area — the most concentrated national forest driving in Kentucky.
tip: Yahoo Falls (Kentucky's highest waterfall at 113 ft) is accessible via a 0.25-mile trail from KY-700 off this route. The scenic byway designation keeps it well-maintained.

name: AA Highway (KY-9) Scenic Section
description: The divided AA Highway through the eastern Kentucky hill country has a smooth, well-banked alignment that follows ridge lines for miles — excellent for open-window cruising through Appalachian foothills.
tip: The section between Maysville and Flemingsburg has the most consistent ridge-top elevation and the widest valley views.

name: Nolin Lake Area Roads (KY-259/88)
description: Edmonson County is home to Mammoth Cave and the Nolin River Lake — the back roads through the sinkhole plain and cave country are full of surprising topographic character.
tip: Mammoth Cave National Park (just north) has its own internal road network that's worth exploring. The Green River ferry (seasonal) is one of the few remaining NPS-operated ferries.

name: KY-89 Barren River Lake
description: The back roads around Barren River Lake in south-central Kentucky — rolling karst topography with the reservoir creating unexpected water views through cedar-glade forests.
tip: Lucas off KY-87 has the best reservoir access roads. The cedar glades north of Scottsville are a unique botanical landscape found only in south-central Kentucky.

name: Berea to Big Hill (KY-21)
description: The transition from Bluegrass to the Eastern Kentucky coalfields — KY-21 from Berea climbs the Cumberland Plateau escarpment with a genuine mountain road character.
tip: The Big Hill section has the steepest grades on the escarpment. Combine with Renfro Valley road for a full day of central Kentucky back roads.

name: KY-800 / KY-463 Cumberland River Gorge
description: The lower Cumberland River gorge below Cumberland Falls — a narrow two-lane following the river through shale and sandstone canyon walls on one of Kentucky's least-known scenic roads.
tip: The section from Corbin to Barbourville along the Cumberland carries the river through a deep, forested gorge largely invisible from I-75. Entirely undiscovered.

name: Tunica Hills Scenic Road
description: Rare rolling hills in flat Louisiana, tight curves through hardwood forest with bayou crossings.
tip: Watch for deer at dawn.

name: LA-115 Kisatchie Loops
description: Winding through Kisatchie National Forest with pine ridges, creek crossings, and genuine sweeping bends.
tip: Dirt sections possible after rain.

name: Cane River Scenic Loop
description: Loops around Cane River Lake past plantation homes and Spanish moss-draped oaks on winding levee roads.
tip: Early morning light is stunning.

name: LA-28 West Pineville Curves
description: Rolling two-lane through central Louisiana's hill country with consistent curves and very little traffic.
tip: Fill up before heading out—stations are sparse.

name: Abita Springs Back Roads
description: North shore piney woods roads with surprising elevation changes and tight S-curves through longleaf pine.
tip: Avoid after heavy rain—leaf litter makes it slippery.

name: Homer to Arcadia Backroad
description: North Louisiana hill roads—among the state's most entertaining drives with rolling ridges and wooded hollows.
tip: Best kept secret in Louisiana driving.

name: LA-10 Evangeline Trace
description: Traces old Acadian paths through prairie and hardwood forest with long graceful sweepers.
tip: Stop at roadside boudin stands.

name: Forest Hill Timber Roads
description: Tight turns through active timber country with blind crests and surprises around every corner.
tip: Watch for logging trucks on weekdays.

name: Bogue Chitto Scenic Drive
description: Follows the Bogue Chitto River through cypress swamp and piney ridge with gentle bends.
tip: Spring wildflowers are excellent.

name: Saline Lake Corridor
description: Hilly north-central Louisiana route with actual elevation and tight bends through mixed forest.
tip: Remote—cell service minimal.

name: LA-478 Piney Hills
description: One of Louisiana's best-kept secrets—genuine roller-coaster hills in the far northwest corner.
tip: Incredibly underrated.

name: Folsom Country Back Roads
description: North shore farmland and pine forest roads with rolling terrain unlike anything south of the lake.
tip: Horse farms add character.

name: LA-9 Bernice to Homer
description: Traverses the pine hills of north Louisiana with frequent direction changes and forested corridors.
tip: Very little traffic on weekends.

name: LA-126 Toledo Bend Curves
description: Hugs the hilly terrain above Toledo Bend Reservoir with sweeping views and technical bends.
tip: Gorgeous fall foliage in late November.

name: LA-117 De Soto Curves
description: Quiet pine corridor in northwest Louisiana's most driver-friendly terrain with real bends and hills.
tip: Pair with a stop in Mansfield.

name: Mohawk Trail (MA-2)
description: Historic route through the Berkshires with hairpin turns, mountain grades, and legendary fall foliage.
tip: The Hairpin Turn near North Adams is iconic.

name: MA-112 Sandisfield Road
description: Technical mountain driving through the southern Berkshires with blind crests and tight forest curves.
tip: Watch for frost pockets in spring.

name: MA-9 Berkshire Passage
description: Long-distance mountain crossing with consistent curves, river valleys, and spectacular ridge views.
tip: Best driven west to east in afternoon light.

name: Conway Scenic Route
description: Classic New England hill town roads with stone walls, blind curves, and farmland scenery.
tip: Conway is a gem of a village.

name: South County Backroads
description: Network of rolling roads through southern Berkshire hill towns—each one better than the last.
tip: Egremont and Sheffield roads are standouts.

name: MA-116 Shelburne Curves
description: Roller-coaster road through the Deerfield River valley with abrupt direction changes.
tip: River views reward every bend.

name: MA-57 Granville Corridor
description: Winding through the Granville State Forest with consistent curves and excellent pavement.
tip: Granville State Forest is also great for hiking.

name: Washington Mountain Road
description: Steep, technical climb over Washington Mountain with switchbacks and dramatic drop-offs on a narrow lane.
tip: Low clearance vehicles struggle; go early to avoid traffic.

name: MA-143 Chesterfield Gorge
description: Dramatic gorge overlooks and tight forest bends in the hill towns west of Northampton.
tip: Chesterfield Gorge is a worthwhile stop.

name: Goshen-Plainfield Back Road
description: Classic New England ridge road with stone walls, farmsteads, and excellent sight lines.
tip: Very little traffic even on foliage weekends.

name: MA-8A Hawley Road
description: Technical hill-town road with sharp crests, narrow lanes, and authentic backcountry feel.
tip: Locals only—check your mirrors constantly.

name: Chester-Blandford State Forest Drive
description: Long descending curves through mixed hardwood forest toward the Westfield River valley.
tip: Watch for ice in early spring.

name: Otis Ridge Road
description: Roller-coaster ridge road in southern Berkshires with sweeping views and minimal traffic.
tip: Outstanding at golden hour.

name: MA-23 Monterey Curves
description: Rollercoaster terrain between Great Barrington and Otis with authentic driving character.
tip: Slow farm vehicles are part of the charm.

name: Florida Mountain Climb
description: Steep technical grades near the Hoosac Tunnel portal with tight hairpins and sheer drops.
tip: Stunning at dusk—bring a camera.

name: Garrett County Mountain Roads
description: Maryland's western mountain county offers genuine Appalachian driving with steep grades and sweeping curves.
tip: Best in October for fall color.

name: MD-135 Mountain Lake Park Descent
description: Descends from Maryland's highest terrain with long sweeping bends and river valley views.
tip: Incredible fall foliage framing.

name: New Germany State Park Road
description: Tight forest curves approaching Meadow Mountain with technical descent sections.
tip: State park entry fee applies.

name: MD-40 Alt National Pike
description: Historic road over South Mountain with consistent curves and Appalachian views.
tip: Multiple Civil War sites along the route.

name: Catoctin Mountain Park Drive
description: Forested mountain roads through Catoctin with tight curves and hidden overlooks.
tip: Camp David is nearby—no shortcuts through there.

name: MD-77 Foxville Road
description: Cuts through Catoctin Mountain Park with very little traffic and surprisingly technical bends.
tip: Dawn light filters beautifully through the trees.

name: Big Pool Back Roads
description: Canal-era roads along the Potomac with rolling terrain and river glimpses.
tip: Connects nicely with a C&O Canal hike.

name: Sugarloaf Mountain Loop
description: Tight loops around the isolated Sugarloaf Mountain with forest curves and summit approaches.
tip: Park at the base and do the loop.

name: Damascus to Barnesville Back Roads
description: Rolling farmland and woodlot roads in upper Montgomery with easy bends and low traffic.
tip: Nice morning run from the DC suburbs.

name: Old National Pike (US-40) Curves
description: Original National Road alignment with period-correct curves through mountain gaps.
tip: Historical markers at every turn.

name: MD-32 Highland Corridor
description: Rolling western Howard County roads with open farmland and gentle S-curves.
tip: Light traffic except during evening rush.

name: Ridge Road Westminster
description: Carroll County ridge roads with pleasant dips and rises through dairy farm country.
tip: Carroll County has excellent roads generally.

name: Harpers Ferry Approach Roads
description: Technical road descent toward the Potomac confluence with brick-tight turns and dramatic scenery.
tip: Combine with an afternoon at Harpers Ferry.

name: MD-340 Bolivar Heights Curves
description: Mountain gap crossing near Harpers Ferry with sweeping descent curves and ridge views.
tip: Excellent in combination with VA and WV drives.

name: South Mountain Crest Road
description: Follows the Blue Ridge crest through South Mountain State Park with forested curves and ridge overlooks.
tip: Antietam battlefield is a short detour.

name: Grafton Notch Scenic Byway (ME-26)
description: Spectacular mountain notch drive through the Mahoosuc Range with waterfalls, cliffs, and dramatic curves.
tip: Stop at Screw Auger Falls—worth every minute.

name: ME-2 Rangeley Region Curves
description: Traverses the western Maine mountains with lake views, forest corridors, and Appalachian mountain character.
tip: Rangeley Lake views are stunning in fall.

name: ME-17 Height of Land
description: Climbs to the dramatic Height of Land overlook above Mooselookmeguntic Lake—one of New England's finest drives.
tip: The overlook is one of Maine's most spectacular viewpoints.

name: Acadia National Park Loop Road
description: Famous 27-mile Park Loop Road through Acadia with sea cliff curves, Cadillac Mountain, and boulder-strewn shores.
tip: Drive clockwise—one-way sections favor this direction.

name: Cadillac Mountain Summit Road
description: Tight switchbacks climbing to the summit of the highest point on the East Coast, with sweeping Atlantic views.
tip: First sunrise in the US from the summit—if you can get there at 4am.

name: ME-15 Guilford to Greenville
description: Approaches Moosehead Lake through the Maine wilderness with excellent Appalachian curves.
tip: Moose sightings are common at dusk.

name: Moosehead Lake Circumference
description: Circles Maine's largest lake through remote wilderness with lakeshore curves and mountain backdrops.
tip: Two-day drive with overnight in Greenville.

name: ME-201 Kennebec Gorge
description: Follows the Kennebec River northward through rugged gorge terrain with long sweeping curves.
tip: Arnold's 1775 Quebec expedition route.

name: ME-4 Sandy River Valley
description: Follows the Sandy River through classic New England farmland with covered bridges and gentle curves.
tip: Covered bridges at New Portland are a must-see.

name: ME-11 Aroostook County Climb
description: Long highway through northern Maine's wilderness highlands—surprisingly technical near Aroostook State Park.
tip: Bring moose-alert awareness—seriously.

name: Evans Notch Road (ME-113)
description: Tight notch road through the White Mountain National Forest on the NH/ME border—seasonally closed.
tip: Closed in winter; check WMNF closures.

name: Sugarloaf Access Road
description: Steep access road to Maine's second-highest peak with switchbacks and dramatic mountain views.
tip: Ski area access; verify seasonal access for non-skiers.

name: ME-27 Eustis Ridge
description: Climbs through the Chain of Ponds region in remote western Maine—empty roads and mountain drama.
tip: Canada is very close—don't accidentally cross.

name: ME-156 Brownfield Bog Road
description: Roller-coaster rural road through Oxford County farmland with great morning driving character.
tip: Combine with Fryeburg Fair in October.

name: ME-35 Lakes Region Curves
description: Winds through the Maine Lakes Region with consistent curves and lake glimpses.
tip: Long Lake views near Bridgton are superb.

name: M-119 Tunnel of Trees
description: Michigan's most beloved drive—a narrow two-lane snaking through arching hardwood canopy above Lake Michigan bluffs.
tip: Blind crests and oncoming traffic demand full attention.

name: M-22 Leelanau Peninsula Loop
description: Circles the wine-country Leelanau Peninsula with dune overlooks, cherry orchards, and Lake Michigan vistas.
tip: Fall colors peak in mid-October here.

name: Brockway Mountain Drive
description: Highest road in the Midwest with stunning copper country panoramas and sweeping curves along the ridge.
tip: Hawk migration peak in September is spectacular.

name: M-28 Porcupine Mountains Corridor
description: Traces the south shore of Lake Superior past the Porcupine Mountains with dramatic fall foliage.
tip: Side trip to Lake of the Clouds overlook is mandatory.

name: M-35 Iron Mountain Drives
description: Up and over the iron range with forested curves and occasional open ridge views.
tip: Combine with a Fumee Lake Natural Area stop.

name: Lake Linden Shore Road
description: Hugs the Torch Lake shoreline through the copper country with tight curves and turquoise water views.
tip: Torch Lake is Michigan's clearest lake.

name: M-26 Copper Country Trail
description: Coastal cliff road along Lake Superior's Keweenaw shore with dramatic geology and twisting curves.
tip: Eagle Harbor lighthouse is worth the stop.

name: US-31 Petoskey Shore Drive
description: Shoreline drive with bluff overlooks and natural curves following Little Traverse Bay.
tip: Hemingway country—visit Walloon Lake.

name: Pierce Stocking Scenic Drive
description: Compact loop through Sleeping Bear Dunes with breathtaking Lake Michigan overlooks and forested bends.
tip: Dune overlook at stop 9 is unmissable.

name: M-64 Ontonagon Coast
description: Remote Lake Superior shoreline drive through the western UP with forested curves and cliff overlooks.
tip: Almost no traffic on weekdays.

name: M-123 Tahquamenon Falls Road
description: Wilderness road to Tahquamenon Falls through boreal forest with classic UP remoteness.
tip: Don't skip the upper AND lower falls.

name: US-41 Keweenaw Peninsula Run
description: Spine of the Keweenaw Peninsula with old copper country character, forests, and consistent curves.
tip: The entire peninsula rewards slow exploration.

name: M-28 Whitefish Point Road
description: Northernmost Michigan drive to Whitefish Point lighthouse through boreal spruce forest.
tip: Edmund Fitzgerald country—great bird observatory.

name: Blue Star Highway M-63
description: Vintage US-66 parallel road through orchard and dune country with old-school roadtrip character.
tip: Fruit stands open May through October.

name: M-72 Traverse City to Kalkaska
description: Forested two-lane through the Antrim County hills with consistent rolling curves.
tip: Trout streams run alongside for much of the route.

name: North Shore Scenic Drive (US-61)
description: The crown jewel of Minnesota driving—follows Lake Superior's rugged north shore through basalt cliffs, waterfalls, and forests.
tip: Split Rock Lighthouse, Gooseberry Falls, and Lutsen are must-stops.

name: Gunflint Trail (Cook County Road 12)
description: Penetrates the Boundary Waters wilderness with lake country curves and boreal forest tunnels.
tip: The end of the road at Saganaga Lake is worth every mile.

name: Lutsen Mountain Access Road
description: Short but dramatic climb into the Sawtooth Mountains above Lake Superior with tight hairpins.
tip: Fall panoramas from the top are extraordinary.

name: MN-61 Palisade Head Corridor
description: Dramatic section of the North Shore with basalt palisade cliffs rising 350 feet above Lake Superior.
tip: Palisade Head is the best rock climbing site in the Midwest.

name: MN-1 Ely Wilderness Road
description: Deep wilderness highway to Ely—gateway to the BWCA—through boreal forest with remote character.
tip: Moose crossings are genuinely common here.

name: Grand Portage to Hovland Road
description: Northernmost section of MN-61 with dramatic coastal bends above Lake Superior's wildest shoreline.
tip: Last turn before Canada—savor it.

name: Root River Valley Road
description: Southeast Minnesota's karst bluff country—narrow valley roads with dramatic limestone walls and river crossings.
tip: Lanesboro is a perfect overnight stop.

name: MN-16 Bluff Country Corridor
description: Follows the Root River through Mississippi bluff country with dramatic curves below limestone cliffs.
tip: An underrated alternative to Wisconsin's Great River Road.

name: Great River Road Red Wing-Wabasha
description: Classic Mississippi River bluffs drive with lake-effect geology and sweeping river views.
tip: Red Wing has excellent parking overlooks.

name: US-169 Iron Range Corridor
description: Iron Range highway through taconite hills and boreal forest with long sweeping bends.
tip: Open pit mines along the way are industrial art.

name: Sawtooth Mountain Byway
description: Climbs into the Sawtooth Mountains above Tofte with forested curves and Lake Superior panoramas.
tip: The view from the top rivals anything in the Appalachians.

name: MN-200 Northern Pine Corridor
description: Remote northern Minnesota highway through pristine pine forest with gentle rolling terrain.
tip: Mississippi River headwaters are nearby at Itasca State Park.

name: MN-1 Isabella Wilderness
description: Isolated wilderness section through the Superior National Forest with boreal character.
tip: One of the most remote drives in the lower 48.

name: MN-23 Driftless Area Loop
description: Driftless zone roads with exceptional bluff views—some of Minnesota's most dramatic non-lake landscapes.
tip: The unglaciated terrain creates genuinely steep roads.

name: Cook County Road 7 Back Roads
description: County roads dipping into river valleys north of Grand Marais with excellent fall color and minimal traffic.
tip: If you find yourself lost, that's fine—you're still in paradise.

name: MO-19 Current River Corridor
description: Ozark river road with dramatic dolomite bluffs, Ozark Springs, and technical winding character through the heart of Missouri's wild country.
tip: Eminence is the best river access point.

name: US-60 Ozark Mountain Corridor
description: Traverses the high Ozarks with deep valley views, ridgeline curves, and genuine elevation change.
tip: Alton has views across the North Fork valley.

name: MO-76 Lake Taneycomo Bluff Road
description: Ozark lakeside road above Taneycomo with dramatic bluff curves and White River gorge views.
tip: Avoid the Branson strip—this is the real drive.

name: MO-H Big Creek Road
description: Incredibly technical Ozark backroad cutting through St. Francois Mountains with hairpins and creek fords.
tip: One of Missouri's best-kept driving secrets.

name: MO-21 St. Francois Mountains
description: Missouri's oldest mountains offer genuine vertical with ridgeline roads and forested gorge views.
tip: Johnson's Shut-Ins State Park is nearby.

name: MO-49 Ozark National Scenic Riverways
description: Threads through the Current River watershed with cliff-side curves and river valley descents.
tip: Float trips are available for a different perspective.

name: MO-72 Elephant Rocks Corridor
description: St. Francois Mountains road passing exposed granite knobs with excellent curves.
tip: Elephant Rocks State Park is genuinely weird and cool.

name: MO-7 Lake of the Ozarks Bluffs
description: Lake-level road with dramatic bluff curves and lake cove views—Ozark scenery at its finest.
tip: Traffic is heavy on summer weekends.

name: MO-94 Missouri River Bluffs
description: Hugs Missouri River bluffs through wine country with dramatic curves against limestone cliffs.
tip: Hermann's wine country in fall is superb.

name: MO-J Arcadia Valley Road
description: Some of Missouri's best driving—an incredibly tight backroad through the Arcadia Valley with zero margin for error.
tip: Drive it early morning with fresh tires.

name: MO-B Shepherd Mountain Road
description: Tight climb over Shepherd Mountain—the steepest sustained grade in Missouri with blind hairpins.
tip: Trucks are prohibited; narrow lanes keep speeds honest.

name: MO-E Van Buren Curves
description: Remote Ozark county road with excellent technical character and the absence of any traffic.
tip: You may not see another car for 30 minutes.

name: MO-160 Mark Twain National Forest
description: Long run through the southern Ozarks with forested ridges, river crossings, and genuine mountain character.
tip: Skyline Drive section has incredible views.

name: MO-32 Camden County Hills
description: Ozark lake district roads with roller-coaster character and lake glimpses through the hardwoods.
tip: Spring turkey season brings great energy to these roads.

name: MO-N Johnson's Shut-Ins Access
description: Wilderness access road to the St. Francois River gorge with excellent curves and forested canyon views.
tip: The shut-ins themselves are a geological wonder.

name: Natchez Trace Parkway
description: Ancient path turned world-class scenic parkway—no trucks, no billboards, no intersections. Long sweeping bends through hardwood forest.
tip: Speed limit 50 mph enforced; use it as a meditation drive.

name: MS-43 Bienville National Forest
description: Piney woods drives through Bienville National Forest with long gentle curves and Spanish moss.
tip: Longleaf pine restoration makes this strikingly beautiful.

name: MS-9 Tishomingo County Curves
description: Mississippi's hilliest terrain—rare topographic relief in the northeast corner with technical driving character.
tip: Tishomingo State Park has waterfall hikes too.

name: MS-72 Iuka Hill Country
description: Among Mississippi's most driver-friendly roads in the Tennessee River Hills with genuine elevation and bends.
tip: The hill towns are quiet and charming.

name: MS-25 Natchez Trace Country
description: Parallel to the Natchez Trace through red clay hills with consistent curves and old Mississippi character.
tip: Slower but more authentic than the Trace itself.

name: MS-15 Pontotoc Hill Roads
description: North Mississippi hill country with rolling farmland roads and the gentle character of the Appalachian foothills.
tip: Not dramatic, but consistently engaging.

name: MS-35 Homochitto National Forest
description: Piney woods drive through the Homochitto National Forest with bayou crossings and longleaf corridors.
tip: Longleaf pine restoration is ongoing here.

name: Old Trace Drive
description: Original sunken road section of the Natchez Trace—an eerie, beautiful forest drive on 8,000-year-old path.
tip: The sunken trace is genuinely ancient and haunting.

name: MS-18 Jefferson Davis County
description: Old-school Mississippi county road with red clay banks, pecan groves, and classic Delta-edge terrain.
tip: Very authentic rural Mississippi experience.

name: DeSoto National Forest Drives
description: Gulf Coast piney woods drive through DeSoto National Forest with surprisingly pleasant bends.
tip: Black Creek is an excellent paddling alternative.

name: MS-13 Pearl River Hills
description: Crosses the Pearl River watershed through rolling south-central Mississippi with piney character.
tip: Quiet except during deer season.

name: Tenn-Tom Waterway Back Roads
description: Follows the Tennessee-Tombigbee Waterway corridor with lock and dam overlooks and river bluff curves.
tip: Engineering marvel worth stopping to examine.

name: Corinth Civil War Roads
description: Northeast Mississippi roads through Civil War battlefields with rolling forested terrain.
tip: Shiloh is just across the Tennessee line.

name: Vicksburg National Military Park Drive
description: Historic battlefield loop with ridge roads above the Yazoo delta and Mississippi River panoramas.
tip: The Confederate and Union lines are both driveable.

name: MS-49 Yazoo Hills Corridor
description: Crosses the Yazoo Hills—one of Mississippi's geologically distinct regions with rolling loess bluffs.
tip: These loess hills are found only here and in China.

name: Chief Joseph Scenic Highway (WY-296 / MT approach)
description: Dramatic climb through Dead Indian Pass with switchbacks, 8,000-ft ridgeline, and views into the Clarks Fork canyon.
tip: Pairs perfectly with the Beartooth Highway.

name: MT-78 Boulder River Road
description: Follows the Boulder River into the Absaroka-Beartooth Wilderness with canyon walls and dramatic geology.
tip: Road ends at Natural Bridge Falls—worth it.

name: US-2 Marias Pass
description: Continental Divide crossing at the southern edge of Glacier with dramatic mountain scenery and sweeping curves.
tip: The lowest crossing of the Rockies in the US.

name: MT-83 Flathead Lake East Shore
description: Runs along the Mission Mountains above the largest natural lake west of the Mississippi with sweeping curves.
tip: Mission Mountains backdrop is stunning in every season.

name: US-2 Kootenai River Gorge
description: Hugs the Kootenai River through a dramatic limestone gorge in northwest Montana with consistent curves.
tip: Kootenai Falls are accessible from the highway.

name: US-93 Bitterroot Valley
description: Long valley run between the Bitterroot and Sapphire ranges with Bitterroot Mountain views and wide sweepers.
tip: Most beautiful valley in the Rockies according to Lewis and Clark.

name: MT-200 Thompson Falls Gorge
description: Follows the Clark Fork River through steep gorges with excellent curves and dramatic canyon views.
tip: Thompson Falls has a small dam worth seeing.

name: MT-87 Judith Mountains Loop
description: Loops around the isolated Judith Mountains rising from the Montana plains—surprising technical character.
tip: Views extend 100 miles in clear weather.

name: MT-1 Pintler Scenic Route
description: Named scenic route circling the Anaconda Range through mining towns with high mountain passes.
tip: Georgetown Lake section is particularly beautiful.

name: MT-360 Pryor Mountains Road
description: Remote climb into the Pryor Mountains above the Bighorn Canyon—one of Montana's wildest drives.
tip: Wild horses roam the Pryors; stop and scan.

name: Many Glacier Road
description: Enters the spectacular Many Glacier valley with tight curves under the Continental Divide.
tip: Book lodging months ahead; the views are world-class.

name: Crazy Mountains Approach
description: Approaches the jagged Crazy Mountains through Big Timber Creek canyon with excellent technical bends.
tip: The Crazies are among Montana's most dramatic peaks.

name: MT-41 Beaverhead Mountains
description: High mountain highway along the Idaho border through the Beaverhead Range with sweeping plateau views.
tip: Big Hole Battlefield is a somber historic stop.

name: Blue Ridge Parkway North Section (NC)
description: Northern North Carolina stretch of the iconic parkway—no commercial traffic, sweeping ridge vistas, and perfectly banked curves.
tip: Fall color peaks mid-October near Boone.

name: Blue Ridge Parkway South Section (NC)
description: Southern section near Asheville and Waterrock Knob—highest elevation parkway road in the eastern US.
tip: Waterrock Knob at 6,400 ft has 360° views.

name: NC-181 Grandfather Mountain Approach
description: Dramatically technical climb toward Grandfather Mountain with hairpin turns, steep grades, and sheer drop-offs.
tip: One of the best-kept driving secrets in the Blue Ridge.

name: NC-105 Banner Elk Corridor
description: High country two-lane threading through ski resort country with excellent curves and fall foliage.
tip: Ski resorts mean traffic in winter weekends.

name: NC-215 Pisgah National Forest
description: One of the most technical roads in the Blue Ridge—tight switchbacks through the Pisgah with sheer drops and cathedral forest.
tip: Narrow lanes; two vehicles can barely pass.

name: NC-128 Mount Mitchell Summit
description: Accesses the highest peak east of the Mississippi via a technical spur—tight turns through spruce-fir forest.
tip: Weather changes instantly above 6,000 ft.

name: Devil's Courthouse Road
description: Short but spectacular section of BRP near Devil's Courthouse rock with exposed ridgeline driving.
tip: Hike the half-mile trail to the rocky summit.

name: NC-107 Cashiers Area Curves
description: Crosses the continental divide in the southern Blue Ridge with tight forest bends and waterfall country.
tip: Whiteside Mountain trailhead access.

name: Max Patch Road
description: Narrow, steep gravel-to-pavement mix climbing to the Appalachian Trail's famous Max Patch bald—360° views.
tip: Some gravel sections; high clearance preferred.

name: Hot Springs River Road
description: Follows the French Broad River through the deepest river gorge in the East—technical bends with river beside you.
tip: Class III-IV rapids visible from the road.

name: NC-80 Burnsville Mountain Road
description: Extremely technical ascent over Colbert Ridge with some of the steepest grades in North Carolina.
tip: Locals call it the scariest paved road in the state.

name: Linn Cove Viaduct Section
description: Hugs the base of Grandfather Mountain on a famous engineering marvel—concrete viaduct with dramatic drops.
tip: Last section of the BRP built; engineering is the attraction.

name: NC-194 Newland to Banner Elk
description: Short but incredibly technical mountain passage with hairpins, switchbacks, and sheer drops in the high country.
tip: Budget twice the time you think it will take.

name: Theodore Roosevelt NP Scenic Loop
description: Loops through the Badlands of the North Unit and South Unit with dramatic butte landscapes and bison herds.
tip: Bison traffic jams are real—embrace them.

name: ND-85 Badlands Corridor
description: Cuts through the Little Missouri Badlands with eroded butte scenery and long curving descents.
tip: Golden hour light makes the badlands glow orange.

name: ND River Road (North/South)
description: Follows the Heart River through the Mandan bluffs with genuine topographic relief for the plains.
tip: Far more dramatic than ND's reputation suggests.

name: Little Missouri National Grassland Road
description: Remote grassland and badlands road in the least-visited county in the US with dramatic basin views.
tip: Slope County has fewer people than any US county.

name: ND-1806 Missouri River Bluffs
description: Standing Rock reservation road above the Missouri River with sweeping bluff views and Native American cultural landscape.
tip: Respectful visitor behavior is essential here.

name: North Unit Drive
description: Theodore Roosevelt NP North Unit's scenic drive through the most dramatic badlands landscapes in the Dakotas.
tip: Longhorn cattle and wild horses sometimes visible.

name: Medora Gorge Road
description: Descends into the Medora badlands gorge with technical curves and bison-country scenery.
tip: Medora is a genuinely fun tourist town.

name: ND-12 Cannon Ball River Road
description: Follows the Cannon Ball River through the Standing Rock landscape with gentle bluff curves.
tip: Quiet and profoundly remote.

name: Turtle Mountains Scenic Drive
description: Isolated hill country rising 600 feet above the plains—the closest ND gets to forested mountain driving.
tip: International Peace Garden straddles the border here.

name: ND-200 Lake Sakakawea Shore Road
description: Follows the immense Lake Sakakawea shoreline with bluff views and dramatic prairie landscapes.
tip: Garrison Dam is an engineering feat worth stopping for.

name: Maah Daah Hey Trail Access Road
description: Access roads through the Maah Daah Hey corridor with badlands scenery and challenging terrain.
tip: Trail means 'grandfather' or 'long-lasting' in Mandan.

name: Sheyenne Valley Scenic Byway
description: Eastern ND's most scenic route following the Sheyenne River through forest and bluff country.
tip: Entirely unlike the western badlands—lush and green.

name: ND-22 Heart River Canyon
description: Crosses the Heart River canyon with sweeping views of the badlands transition zone.
tip: Dickinson has good fuel stops.

name: Killdeer Mountains Backroad
description: Approaches the isolated Killdeer Mountains rising from the prairie—360° views from the summit approach.
tip: Named for killdeer birds—the mountain, not the action.

name: ND-21 Bowman County Badlands
description: Southwest ND badlands terrain with cattle range and butte scenery in the least-traveled part of the state.
tip: Absorb the silence—population density near zero.

name: Niobrara River Valley Road
description: Nebraska's best-kept secret—the Niobrara canyon with forested bluffs, waterfalls, and genuine topographic drama.
tip: Smith Falls State Park has the tallest waterfall in Nebraska.

name: NE-2 Sandhills Journey
description: The loneliest and most beautiful highway in the Great Plains—long rolling dunes, ranches, and enormous sky.
tip: Valentine is the halfway point for refueling.

name: NE-97 Fort Niobrara Wildlife Road
description: Prairie and canyon roads near Fort Niobrara with bison herds and Niobrara River crossing.
tip: Wildlife refuge has elk and longhorn herds.

name: US-20 Pine Ridge Country
description: Nebraska Panhandle's Pine Ridge—genuine hills with ponderosa pines and dramatic erosion landforms.
tip: Oglala National Grassland roads add to the experience.

name: Scotts Bluff Summit Drive
description: Tunnel-piercing road climbing to the top of Scotts Bluff—1,000-foot natural monument above the Platte valley.
tip: Oregon Trail ruts visible from the summit.

name: NE-71 Panhandle Spire Country
description: Nebraska Panhandle highway past Chimney Rock, Courthouse Rock, and iconic Oregon Trail spires.
tip: The landscape that guided 500,000 westbound travelers.

name: Niobrara Bridges Back Road
description: County roads dropping into Niobrara canyon valleys with tight curves and waterfall access points.
tip: Best explored with time—don't rush through.

name: NE-61 Chadron Area Roads
description: Pine Ridge access roads with excellent canyon views and ponderosa character unique in the Great Plains.
tip: Chadron State Park has great overnight options.

name: White River Clay Buttes Road
description: Bizarre badlands-like terrain in the NE Panhandle with white clay formations and dramatic valley roads.
tip: Some sections unpaved—check conditions first.

name: NE-91 Calamus Reservoir Loop
description: Sandhills lake country with rolling dunes, cattle ranches, and warm-season driving solitude.
tip: Anglers and ranchers—that's all you'll meet here.

name: Cedar Canyon Road
description: Wild backcountry road descending through one of Nebraska's most remote canyons—minimal maintenance, maximum drama.
tip: High-clearance recommended; check recent conditions.

name: Agate Fossil Beds Access
description: High prairie road to the fossil beds with sweeping Niobrara River bluff views.
tip: Miocene mammals on display at the visitor center.

name: Snake River Falls Road
description: Access roads through Sandhills canyon country to one of Nebraska's hidden waterfalls.
tip: The only road like this in a 100-mile radius.

name: Wildcat Hills Scenic Road
description: Pine-covered ridges just south of Scotts Bluff with prairie dog towns, pronghorn, and canyon overlooks.
tip: Wildlife area has a state park and game reserve.

name: Pawnee Creek Valley Roads
description: Central Nebraska sandhills and Pawnee Creek watershed roads with rolling grass and valley dips.
tip: You may have this road entirely to yourself.

name: Mount Washington Auto Road
description: The most famous mountain road in America—steep 12% grades to 6,288-ft summit, no guardrails, and wind records.
tip: Bumper sticker: 'This Car Climbed Mt. Washington.' You've earned it.

name: Franconia Notch Parkway
description: Narrow parkway through the narrow granite walls of Franconia Notch—Echo Lake, Flume Gorge, and the Basin.
tip: No trucks, two lanes—intimate mountain driving.

name: Crawford Notch (US-302)
description: Classic notch crossing through the Presidential Range with spectacular cliffs and cascades beside the road.
tip: Arethusa Falls trailhead accesses the tallest waterfall in NH.

name: Pinkham Notch (NH-16)
description: Climbs from the valley into the Presidential Range with dramatic cliff-face views and the Mt. Washington Auto Road junction.
tip: Wildcat Mountain ski area has excellent summit gondola views.

name: NH-116 Whitefield Area Curves
description: North Country roads past presidential peaks with rural New England character and low traffic.
tip: Views of the entire Presidential Range are possible.

name: Bear Notch Road
description: Shortcut through the White Mountains with steep grades and a forested notch—closes in winter.
tip: Excellent alternate to the Kanc without the crowds.

name: Wild Ammonoosuc Road
description: Follows the Wild Ammonoosuc River through a remote mountain gorge parallel to the Kanc but far less traveled.
tip: Gorge views are excellent from the roadside pullouts.

name: NH-145 Clarksville Wilderness
description: Far north NH county roads through genuine wilderness near the Canadian border—rolling terrain and forest.
tip: Connecticut Lakes are nearby and spectacular.

name: Lake Sunapee Scenic Route
description: Lake-circling roads through the hill towns above Lake Sunapee with excellent fall foliage.
tip: Mt. Sunapee gondola adds a summit view option.

name: NH-25 Ossipee Mountain Loop
description: Circles the volcanic Ossipee Mountains with lake views and forested curves unlike anywhere else in NH.
tip: The Ossipees are geologically unique.

name: Dixville Notch (NH-26)
description: Narrowest notch in the White Mountains—a claustrophobic cleft in the rock with near-vertical walls and tight curves.
tip: Famous for presidential primary midnight votes.

name: NH-153 Madison-Eaton Area
description: Boulder-strewn hill country roads near Madison with excellent fall foliage and White Mountain backdrop.
tip: Madison Boulder is North America's largest glacial erratic.

name: NH-49 Waterville Valley Road
description: Dead-end valley road rising into the Pemigewasset Wilderness—tight curves through hardwood forest.
tip: Dead end means zero through-traffic.

name: Connecticut River Scenic Byway
description: Follows the Connecticut River valley north through covered bridges, farm villages, and forested hills.
tip: Vermont side is equally beautiful for a return trip.

name: Old Mine Road (Delaware Water Gap)
description: America's oldest commercial road—follows the Delaware River through the Water Gap with cliffs, forests, and tight curves.
tip: No guardrails in sections—keep left eyes on the road, not the river.

name: NJ-94 Walpack Valley
description: Tight valley road through the empty Walpack Township (almost no residents) with excellent curves and Delaware River views.
tip: Walpack has barely 20 residents—you won't find crowds.

name: CR-517 Highlands Area Curves
description: Winding through the New Jersey Highlands with long forested stretches and excellent road character.
tip: The Highlands are geologically ancient—over a billion years old.

name: NJ-23 High Point Approach
description: Climbs to New Jersey's highest point with forest curves and ridge views into three states.
tip: High Point Monument visible 15 miles away on clear days.

name: Green Pond Road
description: Forgotten NJ road through Rockaway Township wilderness with lake curves and forested hollows.
tip: Technically in NJ but feels like Vermont.

name: Ringwood State Park Roads
description: Wooded park roads through the iron mining heritage landscape with ridgeline curves and lake views.
tip: Historic ironmaster's mansion worth visiting.

name: CR-639 Columbia Road Curves
description: Warren County backroad with tight bends and river valley views near the Delaware.
tip: Practically empty on weekdays.

name: NJ-517 Ogdensburg to Sparta
description: Sussex County highland road with mining history and excellent Kittatinny Mountain backdrop.
tip: Sterling Mine Museum is nearby.

name: NJ-565 Sussex Countryside
description: Rural Sussex County road with rolling farmland, horse properties, and Appalachian character.
tip: Best fall foliage in New Jersey is up here.

name: NJ-206 Stokes State Forest
description: Passes through Stokes State Forest along the Kittatinny Ridge with forest curves and Appalachian Trail crossings.
tip: AT hikers regularly cross here—watch carefully.

name: NJ-15 Jefferson Township Roads
description: Morris County lake district with flowing roads through the Highlands lakes country.
tip: Jefferson Township is surprisingly rural for NJ.

name: NJ-173 Pequest Valley
description: Follows the Pequest River through the fertile Warren County valley with gentle curves and farmland.
tip: Pequest Trout Hatchery is an unexpected highlight.

name: NJ-57 Pohatcong Mountain
description: Crosses Pohatcong Mountain with steep curves and excellent Delaware River valley views.
tip: Short but punchy—best climb in Warren County.

name: CR-513 Long Valley Curves
description: Rolling farm-and-forest road through the Black River valley with excellent character.
tip: Long Valley is one of NJ's best-kept secrets.

name: Batsto Area Pine Barrens Roads
description: Narrow two-lanes through the NJ Pine Barrens forest—flat but winding through cedar bogs and pine cathedral.
tip: The Pines are eerie, beautiful, and protected.

name: High Road to Taos
description: Winds through Spanish colonial villages, aspen groves, and the Sangre de Cristo foothills—New Mexico's most celebrated drive.
tip: Truchas and Las Trampas villages are genuine living heritage.

name: Hyde Park Road (NM-475)
description: Climbs from Santa Fe to Ski Santa Fe through dense aspen and spruce with tight switchbacks.
tip: Aspen gold peak in late September—absolutely stunning.

name: NM-52 Black Range Drive
description: Crosses the remote Black Range through Winston and Chloride ghost towns—dramatic mountain passes.
tip: Road quality varies; check conditions.

name: NM-4 Jemez Mountain Trail
description: Circles the Valles Caldera through volcanic terrain, hot spring towns, and aspen forests.
tip: Jemez Springs has good food and soaking pools.

name: NM-152 Emory Pass
description: Crosses the Black Range at 8,228 ft Emory Pass with sweeping views south into Chihuahuan desert.
tip: Views extend 100+ miles into Mexico on clear days.

name: US-64 Echo Amphitheater Road
description: Traverses the Ghost Ranch landscape with red-rock formations, junipers, and sweeping mesa views.
tip: Georgia O'Keeffe painted this exact landscape for decades.

name: NM-518 Mora Valley Road
description: Traverses the beautiful Mora Valley below the Sangre de Cristos with consistent mountain curves.
tip: Mora River canyon section is spectacular.

name: NM-62 Guadalupe Mountain Approach
description: Approaches Guadalupe Mountains NP through the Chihuahuan desert with dramatic escarpment views.
tip: Carlsbad Caverns is a worthwhile detour.

name: NM-55 Manzano Mountains Road
description: Circles the Manzano Mountains through ancient Spanish mission towns with pine forest and mountain views.
tip: Quarai Ruins are a UNESCO World Heritage candidate.

name: Enchanted Circle Byway
description: Complete loop around Wheeler Peak—New Mexico's highest point—through Taos, Eagle Nest, and Red River ski towns.
tip: Angel Fire to Eagle Nest section is the most dramatic.

name: NM-434 Cimarron Canyon
description: Tight canyon road through granite walls of Cimarron Canyon State Park—excellent curves beside the Cimarron River.
tip: Rock climbing on the palisades while driving past.

name: NM-82 Cloudcroft Mountain Road
description: Dramatic 4,000-ft climb from the Tularosa Basin floor to the Sacramento Mountains through 15 switchbacks.
tip: The vertical relief is more dramatic than most Rocky Mountain climbs.

name: NM-150 Taos Ski Valley Road
description: Climbs through the Rio Hondo canyon to the Taos Ski Valley with tight turns and rushing river beside the road.
tip: Gold in the aspens in late September is world-class.

name: NM-78 Gila Wilderness Approach
description: Remote road approaching the Gila Wilderness through dramatic desert-to-mountain terrain.
tip: Carry extra fuel and water—no services for 50 miles.

name: NM-15 Gila Cliff Dwellings Road
description: Climbs to Gila Cliff Dwellings NM through the Mogollon Mountains with over 100 curves—New Mexico's most exciting drive.
tip: Over 100 numbered curves; count them.

name: US-50 Loneliest Road in America
description: Transcontinental highway across the Basin and Range—multiple mountain passes, empty valleys, and the loneliest feeling in America.
tip: Life magazine called it the loneliest road; get the passport stamped at each town.

name: NV-375 Extraterrestrial Highway
description: Alien-themed highway past Area 51 through empty desert valleys with long straight sections interrupted by mountain passes.
tip: Rachel, NV population ~50—the 'Little A'Le'Inn' is genuine kitsch.

name: US-95 Amargosa Valley Corridor
description: Desert highway through Death Valley country with volcanic craters, Joshua trees, and mountain transitions.
tip: Rhyolite ghost town is a worthwhile stop.

name: NV-156 Lee Canyon Ski Road
description: Climbs from Las Vegas Valley into the Spring Mountains through ponderosa pine with sweeping curves.
tip: An hour from the Strip, feels like a different planet.

name: NV-157 Mt. Charleston Loop Road
description: Loops through the Spring Mountains with aspen groves, forested switchbacks, and dramatic valley views toward Las Vegas.
tip: Summer temperature 30° cooler than Las Vegas.

name: NV-318 White River Valley
description: Isolated Nevada valley highway between mountain ranges—almost entirely empty and hauntingly beautiful.
tip: Crystal Springs area has actual water—a Nevada luxury.

name: Lamoille Canyon Road (NV-227)
description: The 'Yosemite of Nevada'—glacier-carved canyon in the Ruby Mountains with jaw-dropping walls and mountain curves.
tip: Dead-end road; the solitude intensifies on the return drive.

name: NV-225 Jarbidge Wilderness Road
description: Approaches the remote Jarbidge Wilderness—last place named in the lower 48—through dramatic mountain terrain.
tip: Jarbidge town has 50 people and two bars. Visit both.

name: US-50 Lake Tahoe East Shore
description: Nevada's Tahoe shoreline with cobalt lake views, Thunderbird Lodge, and gentle curves through pine and granite.
tip: Much less crowded than the California side.

name: Verdi Canyon Road
description: Follows the Truckee River through a narrow canyon west of Reno with technical curves and river crossings.
tip: Very close to Reno but feels completely remote.

name: Ruby Mountains Scenic Route
description: Circles the extraordinary Ruby Mountains—Nevada's Alps—with glaciated peaks and alpine lake access.
tip: Helicopter skiing in winter, hiking in summer.

name: NV-489 Bristlecone Convention Road
description: Climbs to the Great Basin National Park boundary in the Snake Range with Wheeler Peak approach views.
tip: Baker archeological site is a fascinating free stop.

name: Wheeler Peak Scenic Drive
description: Climbs to 10,000 ft in Great Basin NP past bristlecone pines and glacier relict—most dramatic Nevada mountain drive.
tip: World's oldest trees (5,000 years) are at the top.

name: US-93 Spring Valley Road
description: Lonely Nevada highway through Spring Valley between the Snake and Schell Creek ranges.
tip: Deer and pronghorn are constant companions.

name: Kingsbury Grade (NV-207)
description: Steep switchback descent from Tahoe Basin to the Carson Valley—3,000 ft of elevation in 8 miles.
tip: Carson Valley views from the top on clear days reach 100 miles.

name: NY-28 Catskill Mountain Highway
description: The Catskills' main artery with reservoir curves, mountain villages, and Appalachian character.
tip: Woodstock to Fleischmanns section is best for driving.

name: NY-23A Kaaterskill Clove
description: The steepest, most dramatic road in the Catskills—climbs through a sheer clove with waterfalls beside the road.
tip: Kaaterskill Falls trailhead is here—NY's highest waterfall.

name: NY-30 Adirondack Corridor
description: Traverses the Adirondack wilderness north-south through the park's heart with lake curves and mountain passes.
tip: Long Lake section is particularly beautiful.

name: Whiteface Memorial Highway
description: Toll road climbing to Whiteface Mountain summit via switchbacks—longest continuous descent in the East at 4,867 ft.
tip: Lake Placid Olympic venues visible from the summit.

name: NY-9N Ausable Chasm to Lake Placid
description: Dramatic Adirondack route through Ausable Chasm's gorge with consistent curves and mountain character.
tip: Ausable Chasm is the 'Grand Canyon of the Adirondacks.'

name: NY-8 Hamilton County Wilderness
description: Hamilton County—least populated in NY—with remote Adirondack curves and no fast food for 50 miles.
tip: Carry fuel; Hamilton County has almost nothing.

name: NY-28N Newcomb to Long Lake
description: Passes beneath the High Peaks through Newcomb with the tallest Adirondack mountains overhead.
tip: Tahawus—the highest peak—is visible from the road.

name: NY-86 Wilmington Notch
description: Through the Wilmington Notch below Whiteface—sheer granite walls, roaring river, and technical curves.
tip: Covered by avalanche risk in winter; summer is spectacular.

name: NY-374 Chateaugay Chasm
description: Descends through the Chateaugay River chasm in far northern NY with excellent curves and gorge scenery.
tip: About as far from NYC as you can get in the state.

name: NY-73 Adirondack High Peak Road
description: Approaches the High Peaks wilderness from Keene Valley through a dramatic trailhead corridor.
tip: Trailheads for Gothics and Giant mountain are here.

name: US-9W Palisades Skyline Drive
description: Ridge road above the Palisades cliffs with Hudson River panoramas and tight forested bends.
tip: Perpendicular basalt cliffs visible across the river.

name: Catskill Ridge Roads
description: Ridge roads above the Hudson Valley with Hudson views and Catskill Mountain backdrop.
tip: Thomas Cole painted this view; it still looks the same.

name: Shawangunk Ridge Road
description: Climbs the Shawangunk conglomerate cliffs—the best single-pitch rock climbing in the East—with lake views.
tip: Sky Top Tower at Mohonk is a worthwhile walk.

name: NY-97 Hawks Nest Overlook
description: Perches on a cliff 300 feet above the Delaware River at Hawks Nest with dramatic horseshoe bend views.
tip: Genuinely one of the best views in the state.

name: Ridge Road High Cliffs
description: Mid-Hudson Valley ridge roads with long Hudson River views and consistent autumn color.
tip: Hyde Park is nearby—worth a FDR estate visit.

name: OH-56 Hocking Hills Corridor
description: Central Ohio's most dramatic terrain—gorges carved in Black Hand sandstone with tight forest curves.
tip: Old Man's Cave is stunning at dawn before the crowds.

name: OH-555 Triple Nickel
description: Ohio's most famous sports road—wall-to-wall curves through the Athens County hills beloved by motorcyclists.
tip: Locals call it 'The Triple Nickel.' Earns the nickname.

name: OH-800 Guernsey Hills
description: Some of Ohio's best-kept driving secrets in the hill country between Columbus and Pittsburgh.
tip: Connecting with OH-821 makes a full-day loop.

name: OH-7 Ohio River Hills
description: Southeast Ohio River bluff roads with dramatic views of the Ohio River and West Virginia hills across.
tip: The river views at Belpre are excellent.

name: OH-93 Vinton County Wilderness
description: Ohio's least populous county has excellent driving—remote hills, forested hollows, and covered bridges.
tip: Vinton County has more per capita than any OH county.

name: OH-374 Clear Creek Metro Park
description: Hemlock gorge road through one of Ohio's finest natural areas with tight curves and canyon views.
tip: Only old-growth forest in central Ohio.

name: OH-78 Morgan County Serpentine
description: Serpentine county road through Morgan County's glacially-unscathed hills—some of Ohio's best-preserved topography.
tip: Unglaciated terrain means real hills in Ohio.

name: OH-33 Hocking River Gorge
description: Enters the Hocking Hills through the river gorge with dramatic sandstone formations alongside the road.
tip: Logan is a great base for exploring the hills.

name: Covered Bridge Scenic Byway
description: Northeast Ohio route through wine country and 19 covered bridges with forested valley roads.
tip: October covered bridge festival is spectacular.

name: Canal Road Cuyahoga Valley
description: Follows the Cuyahoga River and Ohio Erie Canal through the national park with gentle curves and historic locks.
tip: Towpath Trail parallels the road for cycling context.

name: OH-821 Noble County Hills
description: Premium Ohio hill country driving—consistent curves, no trucks, no stop lights, and forested hollows.
tip: Noble County is an underrated gem.

name: OH-39 Amish Country Curves
description: Holmes County is the world's largest Amish community—rolling farm roads with buggy traffic and genuine beauty.
tip: Harvest season fills the road with wagons.

name: Old Man's Cave Rim Road
description: Tight access road above the Hocking Hills gorge system with dramatic overhangs and recess caves visible.
tip: Go at opening time—it gets very crowded.

name: Mohican River Loop Road
description: Forested river road through the Mohican State Forest with hemlock gorges and excellent curves.
tip: Combine with a night at Mohican State Park lodge.

name: OH-78 Corning Curves
description: Perry County mining country with surprisingly technical road geometry—Ohio's most underrated driving road.
tip: Empty on weekdays; technically demanding.

name: Talimena National Scenic Byway
description: Runs the ridgeline of the Ouachita Mountains from Talihina to Mena, AR—Oklahoma's finest mountain drive.
tip: Fall colors rival anything in the Appalachians.

name: OK-112 Ouachita Back Road
description: Below the Talimena ridge through Ouachita National Forest with tight forest bends and creek crossings.
tip: Very little traffic—forest feels primeval.

name: Winding Stair Mountain Road
description: Climbs over Winding Stair Mountain in the Ouachitas with switchbacks and forest overlooks.
tip: One of OK's genuinely demanding mountain drives.

name: Wildhorse Mountain Road
description: Access road through the eastern Ouachitas with real forest driving and surprising elevation.
tip: Wild horses were historically sighted here.

name: OK-59 Cookson Hills Scenic
description: Through the Cookson Hills—the highest terrain in eastern OK—with hardwood forest and lake views.
tip: Cherokee heritage country with excellent scenery.

name: OK-1 Ouachita National Forest Corridor
description: Southern Ouachita route through dense forest with river crossings and mountain character.
tip: One of the least-trafficked scenic drives in the region.

name: Black Mesa Backroad
description: Remote panhandle road to Oklahoma's highest point—Black Mesa at 4,973 ft—through volcanic lava terrain.
tip: Smallest panhandle in the US, emptiest country.

name: OK-7 Arbuckle Mountains Road
description: The Arbuckles are Oklahoma's only true mountain range—ancient Precambrian rocks with Turner Falls and tight curves.
tip: Turner Falls is the crown jewel.

name: OK-10 Illinois River Road
description: Follows the Illinois River through the Ozark foothills with float-trip country bends.
tip: The most popular float river in OK—beautiful corridor.

name: OK-82 Lake Tenkiller Road
description: Hugs the Lake Tenkiller shoreline through the Illinois River canyon with bluff views and winding curves.
tip: Clearest water in Oklahoma—stunning in fall.

name: OK-99 Flint Hills Corridor
description: Oklahoma extension of the Flint Hills tallgrass prairie—endless grass and big sky driving.
tip: Spring burn season makes the hills glow orange.

name: OK-270 Robbers Cave Area
description: Ouachita foothills road near Belle Starr's outlaw hideout with forest curves and sandstone formations.
tip: Robbers Cave State Park is entertaining kitsch and real geology.

name: Chickasaw National Recreation Area Road
description: Springs, creeks, and hardwood forest in the Arbuckle Mountains with gentle curves and Travertine Creek.
tip: Natural springs bubble right beside the road.

name: Blue River Scenic Route
description: Rural south-central Oklahoma road following the Blue River through ranch land with gentle bends.
tip: Blue River is a famed trout stream.

name: OK-3 Osage Hills Scenic
description: Osage Nation territory with tallgrass hills and the largest privately held osage orange forests.
tip: The Osage are the wealthiest nation per capita in the US.

name: OR-138 North Umpqua Highway
description: Follows the wild North Umpqua River through the Cascades with waterfalls, hot springs, and excellent driving curves.
tip: Diamond Lake at the end is worth every mile.

name: Crater Lake Rim Drive
description: Circles Crater Lake—the deepest lake in the US—atop the ancient caldera rim with vertiginous views.
tip: Early morning with zero wind makes the reflections perfect.

name: OR-242 McKenzie Pass
description: Most dramatic pass in the Cascades—crosses a mile of fresh black lava fields with Mt. Washington and the Three Sisters visible.
tip: Closed November to June; open season is brief.

name: OR-35 Mt. Hood Loop
description: Circles Mt. Hood through orchard country with spectacular volcano views and Cascades character.
tip: Combine with US-30 Historic Columbia River Highway.

name: Historic Columbia River Highway
description: America's first scenic highway—engineered curves over the Columbia River gorge with waterfall stops every mile.
tip: Multnomah Falls, Crown Point, and Rowena Crest are all on this route.

name: OR-62 Rogue River Gorge
description: Follows the wild Upper Rogue River through ancient lava tube tunnels and natural bridge formations.
tip: Natural Bridge near Union Creek is genuinely remarkable.

name: OR-58 Willamette Pass
description: Crosses the Cascades at Willamette Pass with Odell and Crescent Lakes and consistent mountain bends.
tip: Odell Lake is perfectly placid on calm autumn mornings.

name: OR-66 Greensprings Highway
description: Mountain alternative to I-5 through the Cascades with excellent curves and Hyatt Lake.
tip: Much more scenic than the freeway, minimal time cost.

name: US-20 Santiam Pass
description: Crosses the Cascades between the Three Sisters and Mt. Jefferson wilderness areas with dramatic volcanic scenery.
tip: Suttle Lake and Hoodoo Ski Bowl are worth stops.

name: OR-126 McKenzie River Highway
description: Follows the emerald McKenzie River through old-growth Douglas fir with gentle curves and lava country.
tip: Clear Lake is an ancient lava-dammed lake—you can see submerged trees.

name: OR-14 Columbia River Gorge East
description: East gorge section with basalt cliffs, high desert, and Columbia River views—very different from the wet west end.
tip: Rowena Crest Viewpoint is unmissable.

name: Timberline Road (OR-26 Spur)
description: Steep climb to Timberline Lodge on Mt. Hood—year-round skiing at 6,000 ft—with glacier views.
tip: You can ski in July here.

name: OR-230 Upper Rogue Corridor
description: Remote Cascade corridor between Diamond Lake and Crater Lake with volcanic scenery and forest bends.
tip: Nearly zero traffic in the off-season.

name: OR-234 Table Rocks Loop
description: Circles the remarkable Upper and Lower Table Rocks—flat-topped lava mesas above the Rogue Valley.
tip: Wildflower superbloom in April is extraordinary.

name: OR-22 Coast Range Crossing
description: Crosses the Coast Range from the Willamette Valley to the coast through dense Sitka spruce and Douglas fir.
tip: Steep headwalls and blind curves—forest is cathedral-like.

name: PA-6 Northern Tier Corridor
description: Runs the northern tier of PA through the Poconos and endless ridgelines—underrated classic of Northeast driving.
tip: Endless miles of excellent fall foliage.

name: PA-209 Delaware Water Gap PA
description: Pennsylvania side of the Delaware Water Gap—dramatic ridge road with river views and excellent character.
tip: Counterpart to NJ's Old Mine Road on the opposite bank.

name: Lincoln Highway (US-30) Laurel Highlands
description: America's first coast-to-coast highway cresting the Alleghenies at Laurel Hill with authentic mountain bends.
tip: Original Lincoln Highway signs are still visible.

name: PA-45 Penns Creek Valley
description: Follows Penns Creek through limestone valley country with Appalachian ridge backdrop and covered bridges.
tip: Penns Cave is nearby—interesting commercial cave.

name: PA-61 Blue Mountain Notch
description: Cuts through the Blue Mountain ridge with switchbacks and tight forest bends over the Appalachian Trail.
tip: AT hikers cross here constantly—watch carefully.

name: PA-233 Pine Grove Furnace Road
description: South Mountain area drive through Pine Grove Furnace State Park with forest curves and ironmaster heritage.
tip: Halfway point of the Appalachian Trail.

name: PA-184 Pocono Ridge Roads
description: Pocono Plateau roads with technical bends and lake views in the Delaware Water Gap region.
tip: Fall weekday traffic is light.

name: PA-534 Carbon County Ridges
description: Carbon County ridge roads above the Lehigh River gorge with dramatic views and forest curves.
tip: Hickory Run State Park at the junction.

name: PA-872 Sproul State Forest
description: Remote forest road through the vast Sproul State Forest—one of the most isolated drives in Pennsylvania.
tip: No services for 30 miles; bring fuel and food.

name: US-220 Bald Eagle Valley
description: Enclosed by Bald Eagle Mountain on one side and Nittany Mountain on the other—classic valley corridor.
tip: Penn State is at the end.

name: PA-36 Sinnemahoning Road
description: Pennsylvania Wilds territory in the northern mountains with deep forest and consistent curves.
tip: Potter County is the elk capital of the state.

name: PA-144 Allegheny Front Climb
description: Climbs the dramatic Allegheny Front escarpment with views across the Ridge and Valley to the east.
tip: The cliff face is visible for 40 miles from the east.

name: Millheim to Woodward Road
description: Short but excellent valley road through Amish country with creek crossings and ridge backdrops.
tip: Handmade furniture shops are genuine treasures.

name: Lake Nockamixon Back Roads
description: Bucks County roads around Nockamixon State Park with rolling farmland and forested lake approaches.
tip: Best kept driving secret in the Philadelphia suburbs.

name: PA-113 Chester County Covered Bridges
description: Rolling Brandywine country roads connecting 12 historic covered bridges with classic Pennsylvania farm character.
tip: Wyeth country—Andrew and N.C. Wyeth both painted here.

name: Ocean Drive Scenic Loop
description: Famous Newport cliff-and-coast loop with mansion views, rocky shore, and ocean curves.
tip: Castle Hill Light at sunset is exceptional.

name: Narragansett Ocean Road
description: Coastal drive above South County beaches with ocean overlooks and modest curves.
tip: Best at low tide when the rocks are most dramatic.

name: Middletown Vineyard Roads
description: Aquidneck Island backroads through vineyard and farm land with ocean glimpses.
tip: Greenvale Vineyards is worth a stop.

name: Jamestown Island Loop (RI-138)
description: Circles Conanicut Island with bay views east and west, historic ferry landings, and farm roads.
tip: Beavertail State Park at the tip has dramatic granite points.

name: Little Compton Back Roads
description: Rhode Island's most rural corner—stone walls, farm ponds, and Sakonnet River glimpses.
tip: Little Compton Commons is an authentic New England town green.

name: RI-2 Wood River Valley
description: Follows the Wood River through the largest preserved green space in RI with forest curves.
tip: Wood River is a blue-ribbon trout stream.

name: Saugatucket Road Narragansett Bay
description: Back roads of the Narragansett Bay south shore with colonial farm lanes and stone wall corridors.
tip: Stones date from 1700s clearing—don't disturb them.

name: RI-103 Exeter Backcountry
description: Western RI backcountry through Arcadia Management Area with long forested stretches.
tip: Longest wild stretch in RI.

name: RI-44 Chepachet Village Road
description: North Providence into the wooded Scituate Reservoir country with rolling character.
tip: Chepachet is a preserved 18th-century village.

name: US-1 South County Shore Road
description: Classic South County coastal road through beach towns and salt ponds with ocean atmosphere.
tip: August is crowded; October is perfect.

name: Prudence Island Roads
description: Ferry-accessed island with unpaved and paved roads through deer forest and bay farmland.
tip: Rhode Island's hidden island.

name: Portsmouth Heritage Road
description: Aquidneck Island north section with colonial farms, greens, and bay views.
tip: Green Animals Topiary Garden is a RI gem.

name: Seekonk River Scenic Road
description: Follows the Seekonk River through the East Side with tree-lined curves and river parkway character.
tip: Providence's hidden gem for morning drives.

name: RI-101 Foster Wilderness
description: Western RI's rural frontier—long forest stretches with colonial character.
tip: The most rural road in Providence County.

name: Block Island Scenic Loop
description: Loop roads around the Atlantic Ocean island with bluffs, ponds, and lighthouse approaches.
tip: No cars without a ferry ticket—reserve ahead.

name: Cherokee Foothills Scenic Highway (SC-11)
description: Runs the base of the Blue Ridge escarpment with dramatic mountain views, peach orchards, and consistent curves.
tip: Table Rock State Park overlook is mandatory.

name: SC-107 Chattooga National Wild River
description: Hugs the Chattooga River gorge through wild Blue Ridge terrain with waterfalls and tight forest curves.
tip: Deliverance was filmed on this river.

name: SC-28 Stumphouse Tunnel Road
description: Blue Ridge foothills approach to the unfinished Civil War-era railroad tunnel through dense hardwood forest.
tip: Issaqueena Falls is inside—it's cold and stunning.

name: SC-413 Tamassee Valley
description: Isolated valley road below Tamassee Knob with Blue Ridge backdrop and absolutely no traffic.
tip: Truly off the beaten path.

name: SC-130 Long Creek Mountain Road
description: Technical mountain road below the Blue Ridge escarpment with forest curves and creek crossings.
tip: Less crowded than parallel routes.

name: Table Rock Approach Road
description: Tight approach to Table Rock mountain with dramatic granite face visible ahead and consistent curves.
tip: Table Rock is one of the most dramatic formations on the East Coast.

name: SC-276 Caesar's Head Descent
description: One of the most dramatic descents on the East Coast—drops 2,000 ft from Caesar's Head to the valley in tight switchbacks.
tip: Hawk watching at Caesar's Head is world-class in September.

name: SC-215 Mountain Rest Backroads
description: Remote Oconee County mountain roads connecting small communities with real Blue Ridge character.
tip: Mountain Rest is one of SC's hidden gems.

name: SC-25 Dacusville Ridge
description: Foothills ridge road with excellent views of the Blue Ridge escarpment and rolling farm country.
tip: Best for sunrise with the mountains lit from the east.

name: Walhalla Outskirts Back Road
description: German colonial town outskirts with rolling hills and forest approach roads.
tip: Walhalla has great German-style sausage.

name: Price House Road Spartanburg County
description: Upper Spartanburg County roads through piedmont forest with historic homesteads and rolling terrain.
tip: Piedmont driving is underrated.

name: SC-11 Peach Country Curves
description: Southern end of the Cherokee Foothills byway through peach orchard country with mountain views.
tip: Peach stands roadside June through August.

name: SC-178 Pickens County Mountain Roads
description: Pickens County backroads below the escarpment with consistent bends and mountain atmosphere.
tip: Combine with the Foothills Trail for a full day.

name: SC-8 Travelers Rest Foothills
description: Foothills town road with excellent mountain backdrop and cycling-friendly curves at the edge of the escarpment.
tip: Swamp Rabbit Trail connects Greenville and Travelers Rest.

name: SC-61 Ashley River Road
description: Antebellum plantation corridor along the Ashley River with Spanish moss canopy and historic landscape.
tip: Magnolia Plantation's azaleas in spring are extraordinary.

name: Needles Highway (SD-87)
description: One of America's great drives—threads granite needle spires through 3 tunnels barely wider than a car with switchbacks.
tip: The Needle's Eye tunnel is only 8.4 ft wide. Not for RVs.

name: Iron Mountain Road (US-16A)
description: Engineering marvel with pigtail bridges, tunnels framing Mt. Rushmore, and triple spiral curves.
tip: Seven pigtail bridges, three tunnels—one of the most engineered roads ever built.

name: Wildlife Loop Road
description: Through Custer's open grasslands with bison herds, pronghorn, prairie dogs, and burros.
tip: Burro jam is as likely as bison jam.

name: US-385 Pactola Reservoir Road
description: Black Hills highway above Pactola Reservoir through ponderosa pine with lake views and curves.
tip: The reservoir views are especially stunning in evening light.

name: SD-244 Mount Rushmore Approach
description: Tight curves approaching Mt. Rushmore through granite formations with monument framing.
tip: Avenue of Flags at the entrance is unexpectedly moving.

name: Spearfish Canyon Road (US-14A)
description: Limestone canyon drive in the Black Hills with waterfalls, 1,000-ft walls, and tight curves alongside Spearfish Creek.
tip: Bridal Veil and Roughlock Falls are both roadside.

name: SD-87 Sylvan Lake to Hermosa
description: South end of SD-87 through the Cathedral Spires area with granite rock formation curves.
tip: Sylvan Lake is one of South Dakota's jewels.

name: SD-240 Badlands Loop Road
description: The Badlands main scenic drive—through eroded pinnacles, buttes, and mixed-grass prairie with Wall Drug en route.
tip: Sunrise and sunset are the only acceptable times to drive it.

name: Sage Creek Wilderness Road
description: Remote gravel-to-pavement Badlands back road through the wilderness unit with bison wandering the road.
tip: Gravel sections require confidence; high clearance preferred.

name: SD-79 Cheyenne River Valley
description: Descends into the Cheyenne River valley below the Black Hills with wide-open plains views.
tip: Black Hills in the distance are striking from here.

name: US-385 Lead to Deadwood
description: Tight mining town mountain road dropping from Lead's elevation to Deadwood's casino district.
tip: Homestake Mine, deepest in the US, is here.

name: SD-44 Rapid City to Custer
description: Main southern approach to the Black Hills through ponderosa forest with rolling terrain.
tip: Fastest approach to the south Black Hills from Rapid City.

name: US-14A Sturgis to Deadwood
description: Historic biker corridor through forested ridges connecting the Sturgis rally grounds to Deadwood.
tip: During Sturgis Rally (August), you are NOT alone on this road.

name: SD-71 Wind Cave Loop
description: Through Wind Cave National Park's open bison range with prairie dog towns and hawk thermals.
tip: Park has the world's densest cave system beneath it.

name: Centennial Trail Access Road
description: Black Hills back road through Elk Mountain area with dense pine, granite formations, and consistent curves.
tip: Horse traffic is common—be patient.

name: TN-143 Ocoee River Gorge
description: Hugs the whitewater Ocoee River through a dramatic gorge with overhanging cliff curves—one of TN's finest.
tip: 1996 Olympic whitewater venue; the river still roars.

name: Foothills Parkway West
description: Incomplete but beautiful Ridge and Valley parkway with sweeping Great Smoky Mountain views from the ridge.
tip: The completed eastern section is equally outstanding.

name: TN-32 Big Creek Valley
description: Remote east Tennessee mountain road through Big Creek watershed with forest bends and no services.
tip: Nearly no traffic on weekdays.

name: US-321/TN-66 Gatlinburg Corridor
description: Approaches the Smokies through the Great Smoky Mountains National Park boundary with excellent mountain character.
tip: Avoid peak fall weekends—the park is saturated.

name: Newfound Gap Road (US-441)
