description: Crosses the Smokies at Newfound Gap—most visited park in America; get there by 7am or wait in traffic.
tip: Clingmans Dome spur is a 7-mile addition to the highest drive.

name: TN-421 Shady Valley Road
description: Crosses the Iron Mountains through Shady Valley—one of TN's most demanding and rewarding roads.
tip: Locals know this road intimately; follow their lead.

name: US-70 Cumberland Plateau Curves
description: Crosses the Cumberland Plateau through Cookeville and east Tennessee highlands with ridge and valley views.
tip: Fall Creek Falls State Park is a worthwhile detour.

name: TN-30 Fiery Gizzard Road
description: Skirts the Fiery Gizzard gorge on the Cumberland Plateau with excellent curves and forest character.
tip: The gorge trail is one of TN's best hikes.

name: TN-111 Standing Stone Mountain
description: Climbs over the Cumberland Plateau through Livingston with mountain village character.
tip: Standing Stone State Park has a beautiful reservoir.

name: TN-52 Roan Mountain Road
description: Approaches Roan Mountain's famous Rhododendron Gardens through the high Appalachians with tight curves.
tip: June rhododendron bloom is one of the East's great natural spectacles.

name: TN-68 Copperhill Mining Country
description: Through the copper mining district toward the Ocoee with bald mountains from acid mine drainage.
tip: Lunar landscape near Copperhill is hauntingly beautiful.

name: TN-163 Clinch River Loop
description: Loops around Norris Dam and Reservoir through the Ridge and Valley with TVA history and forested curves.
tip: Norris Dam is the oldest TVA dam—worth stopping.

name: TN-416 Morgan County Curves
description: Remote Cumberland Plateau backroad through Morgan County with ridge views and zero traffic.
tip: Morgan County gets almost no tourist traffic.

name: TN-279 White County Caves Road
description: Cumberland Plateau cave country near Rock Island with sinkholes, springs, and technical driving.
tip: Rock Island State Park at the end has excellent waterfalls.

name: FM-337 Medina River Road
description: One of the Twisted Sisters' companion roads through Hill Country oak and juniper with excellent curves.
tip: Medina River swimmin holes are roadside bonuses.

name: FM-187 Utopia Hill Country
description: Classic Hill Country two-lane with limestone canyons, creek fords, and the village of Utopia at the end.
tip: Utopia's Lost Maples Café is famous.

name: FM-470 Medina Lake Backroad
description: Hill Country FM road through cedar and oak with Medina Lake glimpses and consistent technical bends.
tip: Sunday morning is magical here.

name: TX-29 Burnet Hill Country
description: Hill Country granite cross-country through Enchanted Rock country with Lake Lyndon B. Johnson views.
tip: Bluebonnets carpet the roadsides in March-April.

name: FM-1323 Upper Colorado Gorge
description: Crosses the Highland Lakes country through cedar breaks and limestone bluffs with river views.
tip: Inks Lake is nearby for swimming.

name: Ross Maxwell Scenic Drive
description: Big Bend National Park's premier drive—volcanic dikes, Santa Elena Canyon, and Chihuahuan desert mountains.
tip: Santa Elena Canyon at sunrise is among the best scenes in America.

name: FM-170 River Road (Big Bend Ranch)
description: Follows the Rio Grande through the most dramatic canyon landscape in Texas—600-foot cliffs and desert curves.
tip: Listed in Road and Track's 10 best driving roads in America.

name: TX-118 Davis Mountains
description: Crosses the Davis Mountains—the most biologically diverse range in Texas—with alpine scenery and consistent curves.
tip: McDonald Observatory at night is world-class.

name: TX-17 Marfa Plateau
description: Classic Marfa-to-Fort Davis road through high desert grassland and Pinto Canyon approach.
tip: Marfa Lights mystery viewing area is on this route.

name: Palo Duro Canyon Park Road
description: Descends into the Grand Canyon of Texas—800-ft walls of striped rock with tight switchbacks.
tip: Second largest canyon in the US.

name: US-83 Llano Uplift West
description: West Texas high plateau with mesquite canyons, Pecos River crossings, and sparse beauty.
tip: Seminole Canyon has 4,000-year-old cave paintings.

name: FM-2027 Texas Wine Trail
description: Texas Hill Country wine corridor through Fredericksburg's vineyard district with peach orchards.
tip: Harvest season (August) has open gates everywhere.

name: Scenic Loop Drive (Loop 1604)
description: Northwest San Antonio hill country with oak-juniper corridor and cedar canyon views on the urban edge.
tip: The best drive close to San Antonio.

name: FM-336 Camp Wood Canyons
description: Real County FM road through limestone canyon country with river crossings and the classic Hill Country experience.
tip: Camp Wood population 822; genuinely remote.

name: UT-12 Red Canyon Section
description: Easternmost section of UT-12 through Red Canyon's hoodoos—complementary to the Bryce country.
tip: Rim trail footbridges cross the road for pedestrians.

name: Potash Road (UT-279)
description: Runs the Colorado River through the Wall Street potash evaporation ponds with towering red canyon walls.
tip: Colorado River rapids visible from the road.

name: UT-313 Dead Horse Point Road
description: Leads to one of the world's most photographed overlooks—2,000-ft sheer drop above the Colorado.
tip: Stay for sunset—the potash evaporation ponds glow neon blue.

name: Mirror Lake Highway (UT-150)
description: Climbs to 10,700 ft through the Uinta Mountains—Utah's highest range—with alpine lakes and tundra.
tip: Closed November to Memorial Day.

name: UT-24 Capitol Reef Waterpocket Fold
description: Runs through the Waterpocket Fold monocline with 100-mile rock ridge views—geology made visible.
tip: Fremont Indian petroglyph site is roadside.

name: Zion Canyon Scenic Drive
description: Enters Zion Canyon through the 1.1-mile Mt. Carmel Tunnel with switchbacks and canyon views.
tip: Personal vehicles prohibited in peak season—use the shuttle bus.

name: UT-14 Cedar Breaks Approach
description: Climbs to Cedar Breaks National Monument at 10,000 ft through aspen forests and volcanic terrain.
tip: Natural amphitheater rivals Bryce Canyon with far fewer crowds.

name: UT-128 Castle Valley Road
description: Follows the Colorado River past Castle Valley towers and Fisher Towers—cinema landscape.
tip: Castleton Tower appears in 50 films.

name: UT-211 Needles District Road
description: Approaches Canyonlands' Needles through Indian Creek—the world's best crack climbing corridor.
tip: Newspaper Rock is one of North America's finest petroglyph sites.

name: Flaming Gorge Dam Road
description: Sweeping curves above Flaming Gorge Reservoir with dramatic Red Canyon views.
tip: Red Canyon visitor center has a glass-floored observation deck.

name: UT-143 Bryce Canyon Loop
description: Loops through the Paunsaugunt Plateau above Bryce Canyon with ponderosa pine and volcanic meadows.
tip: Complements the Bryce rim road well.

name: Bear Lake Scenic Drive
description: Circles Bear Lake—the Caribbean Sea of the Rockies with impossible turquoise water—through resort towns.
tip: Fresh raspberry shakes at every roadside stand.

name: UT-153 Beaver Canyon Road
description: Climbs through the Tushar Mountains—often overlooked but among Utah's most beautiful volcanic ranges.
tip: Highest paved road in Utah at one point.

name: VA-56 Back Creek Valley
description: One of Virginia's finest driving roads—crosses three Blue Ridge ridges with technical sections and mountain views.
tip: Blue Ridge Parkway junction at Tye River Gap.

name: VA-33 Swift Run Gap
description: Crosses the Blue Ridge at Swift Run Gap with dramatic descent curves and Shenandoah Valley views.
tip: Skyline Drive junction makes this a natural loop.

name: Blue Ridge Parkway Virginia
description: Virginia's 217-mile stretch of the legendary parkway with Mabry Mill, Smart View, and rocky knob overlooks.
tip: Mabry Mill in fall is one of Virginia's most photographed scenes.

name: VA-16 Mt. Rogers Approach
description: Approaches Virginia's highest peak through the New River Valley with Appalachian Trail crossings.
tip: Wild ponies on Grayson Highlands are visible from road.

name: VA-42 Brocks Gap Road
description: Technical Appalachian ridge crossing with limestone outcrops and excellent fall color in Brocks Gap.
tip: Massanutten Mountain ridge views are exceptional.

name: VA-600 Dickey Ridge Road
description: Below the Skyline Drive with Shenandoah River valley views and excellent mountain character.
tip: Few tourists come down here—it's the locals' route.

name: US-250 Afton Mountain
description: Climbs Afton Mountain with tight bends and Shenandoah Valley panoramas on the descent.
tip: Old route below the I-64 tunnel is the scenic version.

name: VA-231 Madison County Backroads
description: Blue Ridge foothills road through winery country with mountain backdrop and consistent curves.
tip: Barboursville Vineyards is nearby.

name: VA-39 Warm Springs Gorge
description: Bath County's finest road—follows the Jackson River through a narrow limestone gorge with waterfall views.
tip: Warm Springs Pools are 2,000-year-old Roman-style thermal baths.

name: US-340 Luray Caverns Approach
description: Shenandoah Valley road framed by Massanutten and Blue Ridge with consistent river curves.
tip: Massanutten has unexpectedly technical roads inside.

name: US-11 Valley Pike
description: Original Valley Turnpike—Stonewall Jackson's road—through the Shenandoah with consistent mountain backdrop.
tip: Civil War history at every mile marker.

name: VA-610 Back Mountain Road
description: Technical Augusta County back road crossing multiple Appalachian ridges—very little known to outsiders.
tip: One of Virginia's best-kept secrets.

name: Sugar Grove Mountain Road
description: Traverses the Virginia Highlands with authentic Appalachian mountain character and fall color.
tip: The drive from Marion to Trout Dale is excellent.

name: Garth Road Blue Ridge Foothills
description: Wine country foothills roads near Charlottesville with Blue Ridge backdrop and rolling vineyard scenery.
tip: Early morning is when the light catches the mountains.

name: VT-108 Stowe Mountain Road
description: Tight, steep approach to Smugglers Notch from the Stowe side—barely two cars wide through sheer cliffs.
tip: Smugglers Notch complements well from this approach.

name: VT-17 Appalachian Gap
description: One of Vermont's steepest passes—tight switchbacks over the Green Mountains at Appalachian Gap.
tip: 20% grade on the west side—respect it.

name: VT-12 Granville Gulf
description: Drops through the Granville Gulf State Reservation—a natural gorge with waterfalls beside the road.
tip: Moss Glen Falls is roadside and stunning.

name: VT-100 Mad River Valley
description: Vermont's most famous back road—runs through the Mad River Valley with ski resort towns and classic scenery.
tip: Mad River Glen's ski cult begins here.

name: VT-4 Killington Gap
description: Crosses the Green Mountains at Sherburne Pass with tight curves and Killington resort backdrop.
tip: Pico Ski Area has a gondola for leaf-peeping.

name: VT-125 Middlebury Gap
description: Among Vermont's most technical passes—crosses the Green Mountain crest with extremely tight curves.
tip: Robert Frost Trail is nearby.

name: VT-9 Hogback Mountain Scenic
description: Crosses the southern Green Mountains past Hogback Mountain with 100-mile views west to New York.
tip: Hogback Mountain ski area has a great lookout tower.

name: VT-73 Brandon Gap
description: Less-traveled Green Mountain crossing through Brandon Gap with forested curves and stream-side driving.
tip: Brandon Gap is quieter than Middlebury or App Gap.

name: VT-14 White River Valley
description: Follows the White River through a classic Vermont valley with covered bridges, covered bridges, and more covered bridges.
tip: 10 covered bridges along this route.

name: VT-30 West River Valley
description: The quintessential Vermont country road—stone villages, farms, and forested valley curves.
tip: Newfane is the most photographed Vermont village.

name: VT-302 Groton State Forest
description: Through the vast Groton State Forest with lake-view curves and dense fall foliage.
tip: Peacham Bog is a rare Atlantic white cedar swamp.

name: US-2 Winooski River Gorge
description: Follows the Winooski River through its gorge east of Montpelier with consistent gentle bends.
tip: Water gap near Marshfield is especially beautiful.

name: VT-58 Hazen's Notch
description: Seldom-traveled notch road in the far north—closed most of the year and spectacular when open.
tip: One of Vermont's least-known notch roads.

name: VT-16 Barton to Irasburg
description: Northeast Kingdom back road with rolling hills, farms, and the feel of remote 1950s Vermont.
tip: Northeast Kingdom is Vermont before Vermont became Vermont.

name: North Cascades Highway (WA-20)
description: America's most dramatic mountain highway—crosses two passes through the granite peaks of the North Cascades.
tip: Washington Pass Overlook is a short hike to absolute perfection.

name: Sunrise Road (Mt. Rainier)
description: Climbs to 6,400 ft Sunrise—the highest road in Washington—with absolute Rainier glacier close-ups.
tip: Rainier's summit fills the entire sky from Sunrise.

name: Stevens Canyon Road (Rainier)
description: Stevens Canyon entrance with dramatic granite walls and consistent curves below Rainier's south slope.
tip: The Box Canyon pullout is a must-stop.

name: US-2 Stevens Pass
description: Crosses the Cascades at Stevens Pass through Tumwater Canyon beside the Wenatchee River—one of the Cascades' most beautiful passes.
tip: Tumwater Canyon section (May to October) is extraordinary.

name: WA-410 Chinook Pass
description: Crosses the Cascades at Chinook Pass with meadow wildflowers, Rainier views, and Naches River canyon.
tip: Crystal Mountain ski resort is the spur road.

name: US-12 White Pass
description: Southern Cascades crossing near Mt. Adams and Rainier through the William O. Douglas Wilderness.
tip: Rimrock Lake section has excellent fall color.

name: WA-542 Mt. Baker Highway
description: Terminates at Artist Point—the most photographed viewpoint in Washington, with Baker and Shuksan overhead.
tip: Road ends at 5,100 ft—nowhere in the US has this combination of scenery.

name: WA-14 Columbia River Gorge
description: Washington's side of the Columbia River Gorge with basalt cliffs, Beacon Rock, and river overlooks.
tip: Beacon Rock is the second-largest monolith in the US.

name: WA-20 Methow Valley
description: Beautiful valley road below the Cascades through the sunny Methow with apple orchards and mountain views.
tip: Winthrop is a western-themed mountain town.

name: WA-504 Spirit Lake Highway
description: Approaches Mt. St. Helens blast zone with progressive ash-fall landscape and volcano views.
tip: Johnston Ridge Observatory has a real-time seismograph.

name: US-101 Hurricane Ridge Road
description: Climbs to Hurricane Ridge at 5,200 ft in Olympic NP with sub-alpine meadows and mountain goat views.
tip: Temperate rainforest to alpine tundra in 17 miles.

name: Deception Pass Bridge Road
description: Crosses the dramatic Deception Pass tidal strait on a 180-ft bridge—most visited state park in Washington.
tip: The currents beneath the bridge are among Puget Sound's strongest.

name: WA-153 Methow Canyon
description: Tight canyon road along the Methow River through walls of dry-side pine and basalt with consistent curves.
tip: Excellent fruit stands at Pateros.

name: WA-6 Willapa Hills
description: Crosses the Willapa Hills through dense Sitka spruce and western red cedar with tight coastal range curves.
tip: Extremely little traffic west of Chehalis.

name: US-97 Okanogan Highlands
description: Eastern Washington canyon country between Okanogan and the Canadian border with canyon curves and orchard views.
tip: Similkameen Valley orchards produce exceptional apples.

name: Great River Road (WI-35)
description: Wisconsin's Mississippi River bluffs—some of the tallest bluffs on the river with consistent curves and overlooks.
tip: Grandad Bluff in La Crosse is the supreme overlook.

name: WI-60 Driftless Area Curves
description: Wisconsin's Driftless Region—unglaciated terrain with ridges, valleys, and dramatic bluff roads.
tip: Most dramatic terrain in the upper Midwest.

name: County Road C Blue Mounds
description: Driftless zone county road with roller-coaster grades and the Blue Mounds monadnocks in the distance.
tip: Governor Dodge State Park is a worthwhile loop addition.

name: WI-33 Wildcat Mountain Road
description: Approaches Wildcat Mountain State Park through the Kickapoo River valley with genuine hills.
tip: Wildcat Mountain has a canoe rental on the Kickapoo.

name: WI-131 Kickapoo Valley
description: Follows the Kickapoo River—most crooked river in America—through tight valley curves.
tip: The Kickapoo switches direction 125 times.

name: Elroy-Sparta Scenic Drive
description: Driftless hills country with rolling county roads and ridge views.
tip: Elroy-Sparta State Trail parallels for cycling.

name: WI-57 Door County Peninsula
description: The 'thumb' of Wisconsin—orchard-and-lighthouse peninsula with bay views and consistent curves.
tip: Cherry blossoms in May rival Japan's.

name: WI-13 Bayfield Peninsula
description: Circles the Bayfield Peninsula above Lake Superior through orchards and Apostle Islands views.
tip: Bayfield's apple orchards make exceptional fall cider.

name: Penokee Range Road
description: The Penokee Range—ancient Pre-Cambrian formation—with fall color and unexpected ridge views.
tip: Copper Falls State Park is a detour worth taking.

name: US-2 Ironwood to Hurley
description: UP Michigan border road through the northern lake country with iron mining heritage.
tip: Hurley's Silver Street is authentic mining-era Americana.

name: WI-55 Wolf River Road
description: Follows the wild Wolf River through Langlade County with forested curves and class IV rapids visible.
tip: Shotgun Falls is accessible from the road.

name: WI-19 Dane County Backroads
description: Classic Wisconsin dairy county roads with gentle rolling and token fall color.
tip: Fall farm markets along US-14 are excellent.

name: WI-175 Kettle Moraine North
description: Northern Kettle Moraine scenic drive through glacial hills with lake-dotted terrain.
tip: Glacial outwash creates surprisingly interesting topography.

name: WI-67 Kettle Moraine South
description: Southern Kettle Moraine National Forest loop with glacial lake curves and hardwood forest.
tip: Ice Age National Scenic Trail crosses here.

name: WI-82 Richland Center Hills
description: Driftless zone county roads with Frank Lloyd Wright birthplace country and exceptional valley views.
tip: Taliesin is nearby—Frank Lloyd Wright's home and school.

name: US-219 Allegheny Highlands
description: Traverses the highest terrain in West Virginia through Snowshoe country with genuine Appalachian mountain driving.
tip: Snowshoe Mountain ski resort is on this road.

name: WV-92 Cranberry Glades Road
description: Crosses the Gauley Mountain into Cranberry Glades—a boreal bog in the Appalachians.
tip: Cranberry Glades is an ecological anomaly.

name: WV-28 Seneca Rocks Corridor
description: Approaches the 900-ft Seneca Rocks quartzite fins through a gorgeous Potomac headwaters valley.
tip: Seneca Rocks is the most dramatic geological formation in the East.

name: WV-150 Highland Scenic Highway
description: National forest highway along the 4,500-ft Allegheny Front with meadow views and consistent curves.
tip: Zero commercial development on this road.

name: US-19 New River Gorge Area
description: Approaches the New River Gorge NP through deep Appalachian hollows with mining town character.
tip: Long Point Trail has views of the world's longest steel arch bridge.

name: WV-39 Gauley River Road
description: Follows the Gauley River through tight gorge curves—the same canyon as the Gauley River whitewater.
tip: Gauley season (September-October) brings whitewater crowds.

name: WV-48 Germany Valley
description: A syncline valley enclosed by thousand-foot ridges—technical descent with geological drama.
tip: The Germany Valley barn red landscapes are iconic.

name: Smoke Hole Canyon Road
description: The South Branch Potomac cuts through Smoke Hole Canyon in one of the most dramatic gorge drives in the East.
tip: Some sections barely two lanes wide.

name: WV-4 Coal River Mountain
description: Climbs over Coal River Mountain through the Appalachians with ridge views and forest hollows.
tip: Coal Country adds historic context.

name: US-50 Old Seneca Trail
description: Historic Seneca Trail route through the Allegheny highlands with forested ridge crossings.
tip: Native path turned trading route turned state highway.

name: WV-28/55 Dolly Sods Plateau Road
description: Climbs to Dolly Sods—4,000-ft boreal plateau with tundra, bears, and the loneliest feeling in the Appalachians.
tip: Not truly suitable for low-clearance cars above Red Creek.

name: Cheat Mountain Scenic Drive
description: Climbs Cheat Mountain through second-growth spruce and fir—the highest terrain in WV east of Snowshoe.
tip: The Cheat Mountain Club is from the Civil War era.

name: WV-32 Canaan Valley Road
description: The highest valley east of the Rockies—surrounded by the Allegheny Front with ski resort approaches.
tip: Canaan Valley State Park has excellent cross-country skiing.

name: US-60 Midland Trail
description: Historic turnpike through the Kanawha Valley and New River gorge country with Appalachian character.
tip: One of West Virginia's most historic roads.

name: WV-9 Cacapon Mountain Road
description: Eastern WV mountain road through the Cacapon River valley with ridge bends and Potomac highland character.
tip: Cacapon State Park has a great Robert Trent Jones golf course—go figure.

name: WY-22 Teton Pass
description: 10% grade over the Teton Range at 8,432 ft—one of the steepest sustained paved climbs in the Rockies.
tip: The descent into Jackson is breathtaking—literally.

name: Grand Teton Park Road
description: Main park road with Snake River bends and the entire Teton Range reflecting in beaver ponds.
tip: Morning light on the Tetons is other-worldly.

name: US-26/287 Togwotee Pass
description: East approach to Yellowstone over the Continental Divide with Wind River Range views.
tip: Teton views from the summit beat anything from Jackson.

name: US-14A Bighorn Mountains North
description: Medicine Wheel Pass at 9,670 ft—one of the highest paved roads in the Rockies with switchbacks and views.
tip: Medicine Wheel is a 500-year-old Native American spiritual site.

name: US-14 Cloud Peak Skyway
description: Cuts through the southern Bighorn Mountains past Cloud Peak Wilderness with sweeping alpine scenery.
tip: Crazy Woman Canyon section is dramatic.

name: US-191 Hoback Canyon
description: Tight canyon road following the Hoback River toward Jackson with whitewater visible from the road.
tip: Popular with rafters; the road shares their canyon.

name: WY-530 Green River Gorge
description: Remote high desert canyon road to Flaming Gorge Reservoir with spectacular red rock views.
tip: Wyoming side has fewer visitors than Utah.

name: WY-70 Snowy Range Scenic Byway
description: Crosses the Medicine Bow Mountains at 10,847 ft Lake Marie with alpine lakes and wildflower meadows.
tip: Lake Marie at the summit is unbelievable.

name: US-20 Wind River Canyon
description: Squeezes through Wind River Canyon—the most dramatic canyon in Wyoming—carved through three billion-year-old rock.
tip: The Precambrian rock layers span half the Earth's age.

name: WY-487 Shirley Mountains Road
description: Isolated Wyoming back highway through pronghorn country with the Shirley Mountains looming ahead.
tip: Pronghorn herds of 500+ are common here.

name: WY-130 Laramie Mountains
description: Western approach to the Snowy Range through the Laramie Valley with Medicine Bow Peak views.
tip: Connects to the Snowy Range road for a full loop.

name: WY-335 Red Desert Rim Road
description: High desert plateau road with the Great Divide Basin and Red Desert's alien beauty.
tip: Last major unfenced desert in the US.

name: US-89 Grand Loop Road (Yellowstone)
description: The Grand Loop through Yellowstone—geysers, bison, hot springs, and mountain passes on the most unique road in America.
tip: Enter at dawn to see wildlife before the crowds.

name: WY-296 Chief Joseph Scenic Highway
description: Dramatic Clarks Fork canyon highway connecting to the Beartooth with Dead Indian Pass and 8,000-ft ridge driving.
tip: Best pairing is Beartooth south to Chief Joseph north.
